title: Staff Backend Engineer, Architecture Engineering: Nonlinear Productivity
description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

As a Staff Engineer, you'll be the technical anchor for GitLab's Nonlinear Productivity team in the US: the person who decides what "proven" means before something ships, and who helps shape what the team builds next, not just how to build it. It's a from-scratch, generalist team with no dedicated product manager — that ownership starts on day one.

Some examples of the problems this team takes on:

  • Cutting the time it takes to complete a good code review — one that still keeps a human in the loop — by half, using agentic solutions.
  • Turning a manual, error-prone release step into an agentic workflow that catches its own mistakes before a human ever has to.

What you'll do

  • Set the technical direction for the team's agentic systems, from how agents are orchestrated to where a step should stay human-owned, and defend those calls once they're tested against real code.
  • Discover and prioritize sources of friction across GitLab's SDLC, driving the fix — agentic, process-based, or both — from a rough hypothesis through to a shipped, measured result.
  • Work across any part of GitLab's codebase as the problem requires, since this team operates like a small, generalist group rather than one scoped to a single service.
  • Apply distributed systems judgment to catch cases where generated code looks correct but breaks under concurrency, at scale, or across deployment topologies (including self-managed, dedicated, and multi-tenant environments), and coach others to do the same.
  • Mentor senior and mid-level engineers on agent engineering practices and distributed systems judgment, through design reviews and pairing that raise the team's collective bar rather than just your own output.
  • Collaborate with the India-based group a few times a week to align on the roadmap, and represent the team's technical progress to stakeholders in the Chief Technology Officer's organization.
  • Serve as a bar raiser for the team's hiring, owning the Technical Leadership round for other Staff-level candidates as the team scales.
  • Own a greenfield technical foundation from day one, with your scope and impact free to grow as the team scales.

What you'll bring

  • Experience building reliable agentic or large language model (LLM)-based systems, including multi-step orchestration, tool use, guardrails, and recovery.
  • Ability to work autonomously in unfamiliar codebases and drive solutions from discovery through completion.
  • Strong distributed systems and computer science fundamentals, including coordination, consistency, idempotency, rate limiting, failure modes, and degradation under load.
  • Proficiency in Go, Rust, or Python, with the ability to read and modify code in the others.
  • A track record of delivering results from unclear or incomplete requirements — able to take a complex, loosely specified problem and decompose it into a concrete proposal of small, shippable steps.
  • Experience designing evaluation frameworks for systems where "looks plausible" and "is actually correct" are different questions, and a track record of raising the quality bar for a team's output, not just your own.
  • A history of unblocking and enabling teammates — through design reviews, technical writing, or mentoring — and of engaging regularly with other teams to find where collaboration actually pays off.

About the team

Nonlinear Productivity — shortened internally to "NLP," with no relation to natural language processing — is one of GitLab's newest teams: a strategic incubation group that reports into AI Platform leadership under the direct sponsorship of the CTO. It's split into a US group (this role) and an India-based group working the same charter; the two sync on roadmap and tooling a few times a week but otherwise run day to day on their own. Solutions that prove out internally are the team's path to a monetized, customer-facing GitLab offering.

It's a good fit for engineers who want technical ownership of something with no existing playbook, and a hand in defining a brand-new part of GitLab from its first commit.

Remote-Global

An overview of this role

As a Senior or Staff Backend Engineer with the Database Excellence group, you'll build and evolve database automation and PostgreSQL as a service capabilities for GitLab. The level will be determined during the hiring process. You'll use Go to automate the full lifecycle of PostgreSQL across GitLab's infrastructure, making database operations safer, more consistent, and easier to scale for databases that sit behind high-throughput, always-on internet services. You'll work closely with partner teams to shape how GitLab provisions and manages PostgreSQL in a fully remote, highly collaborative environment.

Some examples of our projects:

  • SQL Traffic Replay Tooling, which validates upgrades and changes against real production workloads.
  • PostgreSQL as a Service Platform, which provides standardized, automated provisioning and lifecycle management for internal product databases.
  • PostgreSQL Major Version Upgrade Automation, which supports safe, repeatable major upgrades at GitLab.com scale.

What you’ll do

  • Design, build, and maintain Go-based automation that manages the full PostgreSQL lifecycle, including provisioning, configuration, upgrades, failover, scaling, and decommissioning, reducing reactive operational work that currently takes more than 80% of the team's time.
  • Build automation that works across infrastructure-as-code tooling and cloud infrastructure, and evaluate operator-based approaches as the platform evolves.
  • Use AI agents as a regular part of building and operating services, including implementation, review, and reducing repetitive work, while keeping the context agents need in the repository so the whole team can build on it.
  • Build for internet scale by designing automation and services for high-throughput, always-on production workloads, where GitLab.com traffic sets the bar for correctness, latency, and availability.
  • Integrate compute, storage, networking, identity and access management, and managed data services across cloud providers into one coherent PostgreSQL platform instead of creating bespoke setups for each database.
  • Build GitLab's PostgreSQL as a service platform to replace bespoke database setups with standardized, automated provisioning and lifecycle management, so supporting more databases doesn't require growing the operations team at the same rate.
  • Collaborate closely with product management, infrastructure, software delivery, and other engineering teams to design and ship high-performing solutions.
  • Research, design, and implement improvements to PostgreSQL performance, scalability, and data health, helping maintain more than 8 months of operational runway for all critical database saturation points.
  • Review database automation and Go changes from other engineers and contributors, with attention to safety, maintainability, and performance.
  • Document automation practices, PostgreSQL operational patterns, and guidance that helps engineers use and contribute to the platform.
  • Build safe, repeatable automation for PostgreSQL major version upgrades at GitLab.com scale, validating changes against real production traffic before rollout.
  • Operate what you build in production from end to end, using production feedback to guide each iteration.

What you’ll bring

  • Professional software engineering experience working with PostgreSQL in large, complex production environments, including experience building or operating a database-as-a-service product.
  • Proficiency with Go, including designing, implementing, testing, and reviewing backend services.
  • Experience developing Kubernetes operators, controllers, or similar automation for the lifecycle of stateful services, especially databases. Kubernetes experience is one way to demonstrate this skill, but isn't required; comparable experience building database or infrastructure automation is welcome.
  • Comfort with infrastructure as code and core database operations concepts such as high availability, replication, backups, and system-level performance trade-offs.
  • Familiarity with Ruby is a plus but isn't required. Much of GitLab's application codebase uses Ruby on Rails, and being able to read it helps when designing automation that application teams depend on. We’ll expect you to become comfortable with it on the job, not on day one.
  • Strong written communication skills and comfort working asynchronously in an all-remote, distributed team.
  • Self-directed work style with effective organizational skills, the ability to manage priorities as a "manager of one," and alignment with GitLab's values of transparency, collaboration, inclusion, and open source contribution, as well as its operating principles.
  • Ownership of the technical direction for a major initiative such as the PostgreSQL as a service platform, turning an ambiguous problem into an architecture and a sequenced plan that several engineers can execute in parallel.
  • Influence beyond the team, setting the patterns other engineers follow, partnering with sibling database, infrastructure, and platform teams, and growing engineers through design reviews and mentorship.

About the team

The Database Excellence group keeps GitLab’s databases running reliably through proactive health management, operational excellence, and strategic enablement. We maintain operational runway by identifying and addressing saturation points, operate infrastructure through automated and scalable processes, and provide tools and frameworks that help teams build features sustainably. Our primary focus is GitLab.com, and we're expanding our scope to provide database health frameworks and tooling that benefit self-managed customers as well.

As a Staff Backend Engineer in the Developer Experience group, you’ll work cross-functionally to help us identify and improve the engineering experience across GitLab’s internal engineering teams. We’re at a pivotal time in transforming our testing approach and development experience to enable engineers to deliver high-quality code efficiently and with confidence.

Developer Experience currently has six, globally distributed teams of Backend Engineers and Software Engineers in Test. This role will work across the entire group to help us identify and remove the biggest points of friction that affect development at GitLab. Expect to split your time between hands-on coding in Ruby and Go, designing scalable solutions and helping every team deliver. You’ll be instrumental in shaping our engineering culture across GitLab.

This is a highly visible role with strong company-wide support. You’ll be instrumental in shifting our culture and practices toward a cohesive Developer Experience Platform strategy—backed by buy-in and appetite for change.

Some examples of our projects

  • Project Examples
    In this role, you may lead projects such as:
    • Internal developer platform adoption: Build and evolve platform capabilities that make it easier for engineering teams to create, deploy, operate, and scale services on Kubernetes.
    • Kubernetes-based service onboarding: Define reusable service templates, deployment workflows, configuration patterns, and operational guardrails for teams adopting the platform.
    • Developer workflows and test environments: Build development, CI, and test environments that reflect production Kubernetes behavior — including third-party operators and the custom resources services depend on — sequencing CRD establishment, controller readiness, and dependent workloads so engineers get a working environment rather than a partially reconciled one, across both local and remote clusters.
    • Platform reliability and observability: Partner with infrastructure and service teams to improve rollout safety, troubleshooting, service health, resource management, and operational visibility across Kubernetes workloads.
    What You'll Do
    • Lead and grow a team responsible for developer tooling and internal platform capabilities used by engineering teams to build and operate services.
    • Set and execute a roadmap for Kubernetes-based developer workflows, balancing developer experience, platform reliability, security, and operational efficiency.
    • Guide the design of reusable onboarding and deployment patterns for services running on Kubernetes, including workloads, networking, configuration and secrets, identity, storage, observability, progressive delivery, and the custom resources and controllers that services depend on.
    • Make environment bring-up and teardown deterministic — resolving readiness and ordering dependencies between CRDs, controllers, and the workloads that rely on them — so engineers get reproducible environments instead of intermittent failures.
    • Partner with infrastructure, security, and application teams to turn Kubernetes capabilities into simple, well-supported workflows rather than requiring every service team to become a Kubernetes expert.
    • Establish engineering standards, documentation, automation, and feedback loops that improve adoption and reduce the time required to bring a service from development to production.
    • Coach engineers through architectural decisions, incident follow-up, and production operations while maintaining a clear focus on sustainable team delivery.
    • Represent the team with technical and organizational stakeholders, communicate tradeoffs clearly, and use adoption and reliability measures to guide prioritization.
    What You'll Bring
    • Deep experience building developer tooling, DevEx platforms, testing frameworks, or CI/CD systems at scale.
    • Strong hands-on Go experience designing, implementing, testing, and operating production-quality services, command-line tools, automation, or platform tooling. Experience contributing to Ruby-based systems is also valuable for this role.
    • Practical Kubernetes experience building or operating production workloads and platform capabilities, including deployments, services, networking, configuration and secrets, observability, resource management, and troubleshooting.
    • Depth in Kubernetes deployment lifecycle: Helm-based deployment and release management, kubeconfig and multi-cluster context handling including deploying into clusters you don't own, and integrating third-party operators and their custom resources (CloudNativePG, cert-manager and similar) into working environments — including the readiness and ordering problems that come with them: waiting on CRD establishment, controller availability, and custom resources reaching their own definition of ready. Experience authoring a controller or operator is useful but not required.
    • Experience designing scalable solutions that improve engineering productivity, test reliability, development environments, or delivery workflows across multiple teams.
    • Demonstrated ability to provide technical leadership and influence without authority across engineering, infrastructure, security, and product functions.
    • Familiarity with DevOps workflows, CI/CD pipelines, release automation, and production operations.
    • Strong written and verbal communication skills in a remote-first environment.
    • A product mindset with a passion for empowering developers through simple, reliable, and well-documented workflows.
    • Alignment with GitLab values, especially collaboration, iteration, and transparency.

About the role

As a Staff Backend Engineer, you will provide technical leadership across your team and adjacent teams, solving the highest-scope and most complex problems in your area. You will lead large, cross-cutting backend initiatives, drive our modular architecture strategy, and define the standards that let teams move faster without compromising quality, security, reliability, or operability.

This is a technical leadership role that combines deep backend expertise, systems judgment, product judgment, and influence across organizational boundaries. You will work with Product, Frontend, Infrastructure, Security, Data, Engineering Managers, and engineers across product groups, bringing subject matter expertise, and you will do it without relying on formal authority.

Why you’ll love this role

  • Leverage: Your work multiplies across teams. The platforms, standards, and architectural decisions you lead determine how quickly everyone else can ship.
  • Genuinely Hard Problems: You’ll lead the modernization of a large monolith toward modular, reusable, appropriately independent systems — at the scale of a platform used by millions of users.
  • Influence Without Bureaucracy: You’ll shape technical direction across teams through clear written proposals and decision records, and partner with Product and Engineering leadership on platform roadmap and investment trade-offs.
  • Frontier AI Work: You’ll lead adoption of AI-assisted and agentic engineering workflows and define the review, quality, security, and privacy guardrails that make them safe to rely on.
  • Autonomy: You’ll thrive in our remote-first, asynchronous organization, where clear written communication and self-direction are the pillars of success.

What you’ll do

  • Lead Cross-Cutting Initiatives: Lead the technical design and delivery of large backend initiatives that span teams, and identify and remove systemic bottlenecks across product and infrastructure groups.
  • Own Architecture Strategy: Drive modular backend, service, data, and platform architecture. Lead modernization of the monolith and legacy backends toward modular, reusable, and appropriately independently operated systems — while preventing fragmentation and service sprawl.
  • Set the Standards: Define and improve standards for APIs, contracts, compatibility, schema evolution, testing, security, performance, observability, operability, and maintainability — plus the build, test, deploy, release, rollback, and production-readiness practices needed to operate modular features safely.
  • Establish Shared Patterns: Create the patterns for dependency management, data ownership, eventing, failure isolation, service maturity, and operational documentation. Establish Go service patterns and Kubernetes operating practices where they matter to our production estate, and guide Rust adoption where it solves a real systems, security, performance, or supply-chain problem.
  • Own What You Build in Production: Take part in on-call and incident response for the systems your teams own, act as a technical escalation point during complex incidents, and turn what you learn into architectural and operational improvements that prevent recurrence.
  • Influence and Partner: Shape technical direction across teams without formal authority, and partner with Product and Engineering leadership on platform-level roadmap decisions and investment trade-offs.
  • Grow Engineers: Mentor Senior and Intermediate engineers, shepherd technical debt reduction and reusable patterns that improve throughput, and raise the technical capability of the wider team.
  • Lead AI Adoption: Lead team-level adoption of AI-assisted and agentic workflows, including the quality, security, privacy, and operational guardrails, and help engineers direct, validate, reject, and course-correct agent output.

What you’ll bring

  • Cross-Team Technical Leadership: A sustained record of technical leadership across more than one team or a broad product area.
  • Deep Architecture Experience: Deep backend architecture and production experience in complex applications, services, or platforms, including scaling or governing APIs, service platforms, data systems, modular monoliths, or shared backend components.
  • Modularization in Production: Experience modernizing a monolith or legacy backend architecture in production, and with modular architecture such as bounded contexts, package encapsulation, ports and adapters, service extraction, event-driven boundaries, or an equivalent approach.
  • Influence Without Authority: A strong ability to create alignment through clear written proposals and decision records, so decisions are documented, understood, and adopted without constant escalation.
  • Product Judgment: The ability to balance customer outcomes, delivery speed, technical health, reliability, and long-term platform investment.
  • Mentorship: Experience mentoring engineers and shaping standards through code review, documentation, and example.
  • Agentic AI Leadership: Production experience with AI-assisted or agentic engineering workflows, including the ability to evaluate and improve how a team adopts them.

Helpful experience

  • Go services and APIs at scale.
  • Kubernetes and cloud-native operations, including deployment, scaling, observability, rollback, and production readiness.
  • Rust adoption or production ownership for systems, security, performance, or platform components.
  • Ruby/Rails modularization and large-monolith modernization.
  • PostgreSQL scaling, data partitioning, queues, messaging, or distributed systems.
  • Security-sensitive product or software supply chain engineering.
  • Experience across SaaS, single-tenant, self-managed, or air-gapped deployment constraints.

description:

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

As a Staff Backend Engineer on GitLab's Security Factory: Code Scanning team, you help developers find and fix security issues. Those issues live in the code they write, and you set the technical direction for the static analysis engine that finds them.

Your work spans two complementary parts of a complete security analysis. On the engine side, you shape how the static analysis toolkit models a program: parsing source into intermediate representations, resolving symbols, building call graphs, and tracking tainted data across files and languages. You define the architecture and specifications the team builds against, and you delegate component specifications within them to engineers and to the AI agents that implement them. On the evaluation side, you build and apply tooling that tests, measures, and validates what the engine finds against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities.

What the engine can model and how we measure what it finds are parts of one picture. As a Staff engineer you hold that picture, shape the long-range technical goals of the team, and raise the bar for every engineer on it. We build the engine with AI agents that write and review code from written specifications, under human direction. We expect you to direct that work effectively and with good judgment, and to help the team do the same.

What you do

  • Act as the directly responsible individual (DRI) for the team's highest-scope initiatives from design through delivery, shipping large features with minimal guidance and shaping the long-range goals of the team
  • Bring systems built by one engineer to team ownership through documentation, tests, and shared review
  • Set the technical direction for the AI-assisted tooling that implements, reviews, and validates engine changes and findings, design the checks that decide whether an agent-written change or generated result is fit to merge, and measure detection quality against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities, raising the bar for what counts as a trustworthy result. That includes static application security testing (SAST) rules mapped to CWE and OWASP, and the test fixtures that prove they work.
  • Own the architecture of the program model (parsing, symbol resolution, intermediate representations, call graphs, and taint and data-flow analysis) and of the pipeline that turns source code into findings, and define how both extend to new languages and frameworks
  • Solve technical problems of the highest scope and complexity, actively seek out difficult impediments affecting the whole team, and advocate for improvements to quality, security, and performance with Product Management, UX, and partner teams such as Code Security and Composition Analysis
  • Mentor all engineers on the team through code review and pairing, remove blockers to their autonomy, and shepherd the definition and improvement of our internal standards through review
  • Participate in on-call rotations to assist troubleshooting product operations, security operations, and urgent engineering issues
  • Define the overarching architecture and specification documents for the engine, delegate component specifications within them, and drive their implementation by AI agents and engineers working independently through phased plans, small reviewable units of change, and specifications kept in lockstep with the code
  • Build and maintain the harness, agent instructions, and agentic skills that keep agent-written code trustworthy, including separate coding and reviewing agents, rules and tests the coding agents cannot change, independent review panels of agents from different model providers, and performance, API, and dependency gates, with risky changes escalated to human review
  • Stay current with research in program analysis and security, run AI-assisted research and spikes, and turn the findings into prototypes, proposals, and upstream contributions, including responsible disclosure of findings in open source projects

What you bring

  • Experience building your own LLM tooling, such as a harness, an agent pipeline, or evaluations, with the judgment to know when output is trustworthy and when it isn't
  • Extensive professional experience writing, testing, and reviewing production code in Rust, Go, or a comparable systems language, with depth in at least one. The engine is Rust, the analyzer wrapper is Go, and the monolith integration is Ruby, and we value willingness to work across them.
  • Experience with performance optimization and with containerized workflows and CI/CD (we use Docker heavily)
  • A deep program analysis and static analysis background, such as parsing and ASTs, intermediate representations (SSA, control-flow and call graphs), taint and data-flow analysis, type inference, incremental and fixpoint computation, or writing detection rules, with the ability to read, evaluate, and apply the research literature
  • Deep application security experience, such as vulnerability research, secure code review, or writing detection rules, and fluency with vulnerability classes (OWASP Top 10, CWE)
  • Demonstrated capacity to communicate clearly and concisely about complex technical, architectural, and organizational problems, and to write architecture and design specifications that bring a team to a decision
  • A track record of taking ownership of ambiguous, team-wide problems and shipping them from concept to production with minimal guidance, with specific, regular async updates on progress, blockers, risks, and next steps
  • Experience defining a system's overarching architecture, delegating component specifications to engineers and AI agents, and getting them implemented reliably
  • A track record of mentoring engineers, raising a team's technical bar, and influencing technical direction by achieving consensus with peers and leadership

Helpful experience

  • Familiarity with popular web or mobile application frameworks and how they handle input, data, and configuration
  • Experience designing guardrails for agent-written code, such as mutation testing, fuzzing, and CI gates the coding agent cannot modify
  • A record of engaging with the research community, such as publications, tool papers, or upstream open source contributions in program analysis or security

About the team

The Security Factory: Code Scanning team develops GitLab's SAST capabilities for customer software repositories.

We work closely with the Code Security team on scanning rules & flows, with Composition Analysis on the broader software supply chain, and with other groups across the Sec Section. We rely heavily on asynchronous work across time zones.

The Community You Will Join

Airbnb’s Data Infrastructure organization builds the platforms that power data across the company. Within it, the Data Movement & Transformation (DMT) pillar builds the platform that moves data between Airbnb’s storage engines and transforms it along the way.

Today, data moves through many bespoke, one-off pipelines that are built and maintained differently by each team. We’re replacing them with one unified, declarative platform. You define data once, and it is replicated everywhere it needs to go. This work underpins Airbnb’s Data as a Service initiative.

You’ll join the team that owns three connected layers of that platform:

  • Control plane: the layer that turns declarative data definitions into running pipelines, including provisioning, runtime selection, and lifecycle management.
  • Schema: how schemas are defined, tracked, and evolved safely across every system and engine.
  • Realtime Data Infrastructure (RTDI): Kafka and the streaming transport layer that real-time data flows through at scale.

As a Staff Software Engineer, you’ll set technical direction across these layers and stay hands-on in the code.

Examples of the Difference You’ll Make

  • Design and evolve the control plane that automatically provisions Kafka topics, registers schemas, and deploys pipelines from a declarative definition.
  • Build schema management that makes evolution safe and backward compatible across streaming, storage, and warehouse systems.
  • Improve the reliability, scalability, and cost efficiency of RTDI and Kafka at Airbnb’s scale, including capacity, multi-tenancy, and failure handling.
  • Replace fragmented pipeline tooling with shared, self-serve platform abstractions that other teams adopt.
  • Lead design reviews and incident follow-through, and raise the engineering and operational bar for the team.

Your Expertise

  • 9+ years of software engineering, including significant experience building and operating large-scale distributed systems, ideally data platforms, event-driven systems, or streaming infrastructure.
  • Hands-on experience with Kafka or a similar distributed log or messaging system, with a good understanding of partitioning, delivery semantics, throughput, and operational tradeoffs.
  • Experience designing schema or data contract systems, such as schema registries, serialization formats like Avro or Protobuf, and compatibility and evolution strategies.
  • Experience building control planes or platform APIs, such as declarative configuration, reconciliation, workflow orchestration, or resource provisioning, ideally on Kubernetes.
  • Familiarity with stream processing (e.g., Flink) or change data capture is a plus.
  • A track record of leading ambiguous, multi-quarter projects, taking them from design through delivery in production.
  • Ability to set technical direction, write clear design docs, and align multiple teams, and to mentor and grow other engineers.
  • Experience running large-scale systems in production, including on-call, incident response, and root cause analysis.
  • Writes clean, testable, maintainable code.
  • Strong collaboration and communication skills in a remote working environment.

title: Staff+ Software Engineer, Deployment
region: Friendly (Travel-Required) / San Francisco, CA / Seattle, WA / New York City, NY
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Every change to Anthropic's software has to reach production somehow: new code, runtime configuration, feature flags, infrastructure changes. Our team builds the systems those changes travel through. Our mission is to give every team at Anthropic a fast, safe, and predictable path from change to production.

We sit within Anthropic's Infrastructure organization and own pipelines, staged rollouts, health-gated promotion, and rollback, along with runtime configuration, feature flags, and the systems that deliver code and artifacts to machines across a very large fleet. You'll own a meaningful part of this end to end, from design through operating it in production.

If you want your work to shape how fast and how safely Anthropic ships, this could be a great fit.

Key responsibilities

  • Set technical direction for major parts of the deployment platform and own them end to end: design, implementation, and operations
  • Build rollout safety into the platform, including progressive delivery, health-gated promotion, automatic pause and rollback, and deploy controls that teams manage themselves
  • Design APIs and abstractions that work equally well for engineers and for AI agents
  • Extend the platform to new workload types and runtimes, from Kubernetes to serverless and edge platforms
  • Build and operate runtime configuration and feature flag systems with validation, gradual rollout, and fast rollback
  • Build infrastructure-as-code workflows that many teams rely on for safe, routine changes
  • Scale artifact distribution so code and configuration reach machines quickly and efficiently
  • Partner with Security so that the path to production is secure by default, with verifiable builds, least-privilege access, and auditable changes
  • Work directly with teams across Anthropic to understand their deployment needs and bring their workloads onto the platform
  • Take part in on-call and incident response, and turn what you learn into guardrails that prevent the same problem from recurring

Minimum qualifications

  • Proficiency in at least one backend or systems programming language, such as Rust, Go, C++, or Java
  • Experience leading the design, building, and operation of distributed systems or infrastructure in production, including technical direction across teams
  • Experience with cloud infrastructure and containerized workloads, such as Kubernetes on AWS or GCP
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience building deployment, release, or change management systems at large scale
  • Experience with production on-call and incident response
  • Experience with Rust in production
  • Experience with progressive delivery and GitOps tooling, such as Argo CD or Argo Rollouts
  • Deep knowledge of Kubernetes, including controllers and operators
  • Experience with Terraform or other infrastructure-as-code systems at scale, including state management and locking
  • Experience building feature flag, experimentation, or dynamic configuration systems
  • Experience with artifact or package distribution, such as OCI registries, Nix, or content-addressed storage
  • Experience with software supply chain security, such as signed build provenance
  • Experience building high-throughput workflow engines or control planes backed by relational databases
  • Experience building internal developer platforms and leading adoption across many teams
  • Experience using AI agents in your own engineering work, or building systems that agents operate

Representative projects

  • Build operator controls for progressive rollouts, including pause and resume that preserve rollout state
  • Design a deployment engine built on fine-grained targets and their dependencies, so each change rolls out exactly where it needs to
  • Build cluster-health-aware rollouts that steer around unhealthy clusters
  • Add a new workload type to the platform, including its rollout, verification, and rollback behavior
  • Design a deployment control plane that handles sharp bursts of agent-driven traffic
  • Design a distribution system that delivers configuration and artifacts to every machine in the fleet as demand grows

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$405,000—$485,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

title: Design Engineer, Power Generation
description:
About the Team

OpenAI, in close collaboration with our capital partners, is building the world's most advanced AI infrastructure ecosystem. The Industrial Compute organization develops and delivers the large-scale power, data center, and compute infrastructure required to support frontier AI systems. The Data Center Engineering team works across energy, electrical, mechanical, controls, site development, construction, commissioning, operations, and external partners to turn demanding campus power requirements into safe, reliable, and executable solutions.

About the Role

We are seeking a Design Engineer, Power Generation to develop and integrate power-generation systems for large-scale AI infrastructure campuses. You will translate campus load, reliability, schedule, and operating requirements into practical generation architectures and technical design criteria, supporting both behind-the-meter generation and hybrid grid-and-generation strategies.

This is an individual contributor role with broad technical ownership from early concept and technology evaluation through detailed design, equipment selection, construction support, commissioning, and performance validation. You will work with internal engineering teams, utilities, OEMs, EPC partners, developers, and operators to resolve interfaces, make disciplined tradeoffs, and establish repeatable power-generation designs that can scale across the portfolio.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop power-generation concepts, reference architectures, design criteria, and site-specific requirements based on campus demand, phasing, reliability targets, grid availability, fuel strategy, site constraints, and operating objectives.

  • Evaluate generation technologies and system configurations, including gas turbines, reciprocating engines, fuel cells, battery energy storage, microgrids, black-start systems, and hybrid grid-connected solutions.

  • Define and review plant electrical and mechanical balance-of-plant requirements, protection and controls philosophy, grid-paralleling and islanding behavior, redundancy, maintainability, and operational modes.

  • Translate AI infrastructure load profiles and deployment schedules into generation capacity plans, equipment sizing, ramp strategies, performance requirements, and commissioning criteria.

  • Lead technical diligence of OEM, EPC, developer, and supplier proposals; review calculations, one-line diagrams, layouts, specifications, studies, schedules, and design assumptions to identify gaps and material risks.

  • Coordinate interfaces across utility interconnection, substations, campus electrical distribution, cooling systems, controls, fuel supply, emissions, water, civil design, permitting, construction, and operations.

  • Evaluate tradeoffs across availability, efficiency, emissions, cost, schedule, constructibility, scalability, maintainability, and long-term operating flexibility, and document clear technical recommendations.

  • Support equipment selection, procurement, design reviews, factory and site acceptance testing, construction issue resolution, commissioning, performance testing, and operational handoff.

  • Investigate design or field-performance issues, drive corrective actions with partners, and incorporate lessons learned into engineering standards, specifications, and future reference designs.

Qualifications

  • 8+ years of engineering experience in power generation or industrial power systems, including responsibility for generation facility design or integration.

  • A bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

  • Experience taking generation projects from concept and equipment selection through detailed design, with direct involvement in procurement, construction support, commissioning, or performance testing.

  • Strong understanding of generation technologies such as gas turbines or reciprocating engines and their supporting electrical, mechanical, and fuel systems, including protection, controls, grid paralleling, islanding, and black start.

  • Ability to evaluate engineering studies, drawings, specifications, and supplier proposals; identify technical risks; and make defensible tradeoffs among safety, reliability, cost, schedule, and maintainability.

  • Experience resolving design interfaces across engineering disciplines and coordinating equipment suppliers, engineering and construction partners, utilities, and operators.

  • Sound judgment around safety, reliability, constructibility, maintainability, and technical risk, with the ability to make decisions when requirements or information are incomplete.

  • Ability to document design requirements, assumptions, and decisions clearly and explain technical recommendations to engineering, delivery, commercial, and leadership teams.

Preferred Skills

  • Professional Engineer licensure and experience developing reusable engineering standards and reference designs across multiple projects.

  • Hands-on experience deploying and commissioning onsite generation for campuses or industrial facilities with demand in the hundreds of megawatts or more, including large load steps and rapid power fluctuations.

  • Experience co-designing and deploying battery energy storage systems (BESS) with onsite generation, including power and energy sizing, controls integration, load smoothing, and frequency support.

  • Familiarity with utility interconnection studies, emissions and environmental constraints, fuel-supply requirements, and generation permitting.

  • Experience validating generation and storage performance through dynamic studies and field testing, including load steps, load rejection, generator trips, and transitions between grid-connected and islanded operation.

  • Experience delivering phased campus power, including integrating temporary generation, permanent generation, storage, and utility service while maintaining power to operating loads.

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

title: Research Engineer / Research Scientist, Human Flourishing
description:
About the Team

The Human Flourishing team’s mission is to ensure AI systems understand and advance human flourishing. As AI becomes more capable and plays a larger role in people’s lives, we want its human benefits to grow with its capabilities. The Human Flourishing team is part of the broader Personal AGI organization.

Our approach has two parts. Firstly, we measure and improve models’ understanding, capability, and propensity to act according to people’s values and to help them achieve their long-term goals. Secondly, we directly scale tangible impact for users in human domains like education and mental health, working across research, product, and partnerships to increase the benefits over a billion people experience weekly when they use ChatGPT.

Our recent work includes Beneficial RL, which investigates how training for beneficial behavior generalizes across settings, and MentalHealthBench, a benchmark developed with mental health experts to evaluate realistic conversations.

About the Role

We’re looking for an exceptional, hands-on researcher to turn difficult-to-define signals of long-term flourishing into measurable improvements in model behavior. You’ll help set research direction, build what is needed to test your ideas, and drive successful work into the models and products we ship.

We’re especially interested in researchers with deep experience improving frontier models through pretraining or reinforcement learning (RL) / post-training, especially on less verifiable problems, or researchers who combine strong LLM skills with deep expertise in domains like education or mental health. Prior experience in these domains is not required.

In this role, you will

  • Develop scalable training methods across the training stack that improve how models understand people’s values, support their agency, and help them achieve long-term goals.

  • Lead high-leverage research from an open question to a shipped improvement: choose a hard-to-define problem, iteratively define success, run experiments, and integrate into frontier models.

  • Build RL environments for difficult-to-verify outcomes, and study whether beneficial behavior generalizes across settings.

  • Create evaluations grounded in human expertise and feedback that reveal capability gaps, unintended incentives in RL, and failures that aggregate scores can miss.

  • Test whether measures of model behavior predict better learning, wellbeing, and other long-term outcomes, and use those findings to guide training.

  • Build new 0→1 capabilities in human domains that may have an increasing impact with upcoming increases in model intelligence and test-time compute.

  • Partner with product teams, engineers, partnerships teams, and domain experts to deploy promising methods, measure their effects in real use, and turn what you learn into further improvements.

  • Assess AI’s impacts on human flourishing at the scale of over a billion users.

You might thrive in this role if you

  • Care deeply about helping AI improve people’s lives, and feel this is a responsibility that comes with increasingly capable models.

  • Have an unusually strong research record in pretraining or RL / post-training research, especially in a hard-to-verify area; or combine strong LLM research skills with deep expertise in education, mental health, or a related field of human benefit.

  • Are a hands-on builder who can turn ideas into rigorous experiments, write and debug code, and work directly with data and training infrastructure.

  • Have the taste to choose consequential problems and actionable steps on the path to solving those problems.

  • Take ownership of ambiguous problems and choose methods based on the impact they can deliver, including when the most useful work is unglamorous.

  • Care about whether a capability will scale, generalize, and make it into the real world—not just whether it can be shown in a paper or prototype.

  • Work well across disciplines and can grok the most important bottlenecks to scaling our impact in a multidisciplinary problem.

title: Compliance Engineer

description:

Figma’s platform helps teams bring ideas to life—whether you're brainstorming, creating a prototype, translating designs into code, or iterating with AI. From idea to product, Figma empowers teams to streamline workflows, move faster, and work together in real time from anywhere in the world. If you're excited to shape the future of design and collaboration, join us!

As a Compliance Engineer at Figma, you will play a critical role in designing, implementing, and testing security controls across multiple compliance frameworks, including FedRAMP, SOC 2, ISO 27001, and NIST. You will collaborate closely with security, infrastructure, and product engineering teams to translate regulatory requirements into effective technical controls, evaluate control effectiveness, and identify opportunities to improve security and compliance processes. You will also help advance Figma’s compliance engineering capabilities by leveraging automation, machine-readable control definitions (JSON), APIs, and AI-assisted development tools to streamline control testing, evidence collection, and continuous monitoring. This role combines deep security compliance expertise with technical problem-solving to build scalable, repeatable, and effective compliance practices.

This is a full time role that can be held from one of our US hubs or remotely in the United States.

What you’ll do at Figma:

  • Develop and verify technical security controls that satisfy multiple compliance frameworks
  • Collaborate with security, infrastructure, and product engineering teams to translate compliance requirements into effective technical controls
  • Design and execute control testing procedures to assess control performance, surface gaps, and verify that remediation is complete
  • Establish repeatable control assessments and continuous monitoring processes to evaluate compliance effectiveness
  • Translate security requirements into structured, machine-readable JSON definitions to support control management, testing, and automation
  • Build and maintain API integrations and automated workflows to streamline evidence collection, control validation, and compliance processes
  • Identify opportunities to improve control effectiveness, reduce manual effort, and scale compliance operations across multiple frameworks

We’d love to hear from you if you have:

  • 5+ years of hands-on experience in security compliance, security assurance, IT audit, or compliance engineering
  • Experience with security compliance frameworks, including FedRAMP, SOC 2, ISO 27001, and NIST 800-53, designing, implementing, and testing technical security controls in SaaS or cloud environments
  • Experience testing security controls for design and operating performance, including surfacing gaps and confirming fixes
  • Understanding of cloud security concepts, including identity and access management, vulnerability management, logging, and security configurations
  • Experience working with engineering teams to implement compliance requirements as technical solutions

The Rendering & Animation team (R&A) builds the graphics engine which renders the canvas for all Figma applications. Our mission is to make rendering performant, feature-rich, reliable, maintainable and extendible across all products & surfaces. The team plays a core, bedrock role for the company because it underpins the technology driving the user experience, touching many other teams, and as such is one of the most impactful areas of Figma.

The R&A team is devoted to hiring individuals with graphics expertise. A PhD Intern specializing in any of these areas would be a phenomenal fit for the team with a lot of exciting projects available.

As an intern on our team, you'll take ownership of a high-impact project at the intersection of your technical strengths and our most pressing graphics, rendering, or media challenges. You'll work closely with your intern manager, team leads, and collaborators across 1–2 partner teams to deliver tangible results within your internship. This is an opportunity to do significant, portfolio-worthy work that directly supplies Figma's visual platform.

This is a 12 or 16-week internship role that can be held from one of our US hubs (San Francisco or New York) starting in May or June of 2027.

  • Develop, validate, and document solutions from prototypes to production-ready systems

title: IT System Engineer
description:
Contentsquare is the all-in-one experience intelligence platform designed to be easily used by anyone who cares about digital journeys. With our flexible and scalable platform, organizations quickly get a deep understanding of their customers’ whole online journey.
We are a global leader in the experience analytics space, with a growing presence across 15 offices worldwide. We’re here to stay—and we’re looking for team members who are excited to drive impact and help us scale even further.
Our aim is to create an inclusive workplace where everyone learns and succeeds. Contentsquare has built a community of individuals who are daring, understanding, and deliberate. We invite you to join us in making the complex simpler—for our customers, their customers, and each other.
Important note: Be careful of scammers pretending to be from Contentsquare. We will never ask for money or contact you through random texts. Any communication from our in house Talent Acquisition team will only ever come from our contentsquare.com or @contentsquare-ext.com domain. For more information, visit our careers blog.

About the job

You will join the IT System Engineering team within the IT Department, alongside the IT Support and IT Project Management teams. Based in Paris, you will report to the IT System Engineering Manager and contribute to the design, deployment, maintenance, and continuous improvement of Contentsquare’s core IT platforms. This is a full-time, permanent position with no direct reports.

You will work across identity and access management, endpoint and mobile device management, SaaS applications, automation, and AI-enabled IT initiatives. The role is primarily on-site in Paris, with some remote work permitted according to company policy.

What you’ll do

  • Design, build, deploy, maintain, and continuously improve the core IT platform across identity and access management, endpoint management, enterprise mobility, and cross-functional SaaS applications.

  • Manage and improve Okta, Jamf, Google Workspace, Slack, Microsoft Intune, macOS, and Windows environments, ensuring secure, reliable, and effective services for employees.

  • Build and maintain automated workflows using Okta Workflows, Zapier, Workato, or similar platforms to simplify IT processes and improve the employee experience.

  • Develop, maintain, and improve Bash scripts and other scripts used to automate IT operations, system administration tasks, monitoring, configuration, and user or device lifecycle processes.

  • Collaborate with the IT Support team on escalated cases and cross-team projects, providing technical expertise across identity, endpoints, access, SaaS applications, and device management.

  • Lead assigned initiatives autonomously, contribute to project management, provide clear progress updates, and use tools such as Jira to track projects and deliverables.

  • Use AI tools and set up MCP servers to support automation, IT operations, and the AI at Work initiative.

Outcomes you will work toward

  • Maintain secure, reliable, and well-managed identity, endpoint, and SaaS environments for Contentsquare employees.

  • Improve the efficiency, scalability, and consistency of IT operations through automation and scripting.

  • Resolve escalated cases effectively in collaboration with the IT Support team.

  • Deliver owned projects and initiatives with clear planning, documentation, stakeholder communication, and follow-through.

  • Identify and implement practical opportunities to improve security, performance, reliability, and employee experience across the IT platform.

Operational responsibilities

  • Manage the day-to-day operation and continuous improvement of identity, endpoint, MDM, SaaS, and automation platforms.

  • Develop and maintain Bash scripts and other scripts that reduce manual work and improve consistency across IT operations.

  • Monitor configurations, deployments, software updates, access, and security controls across managed environments.

  • Investigate complex technical issues, identify root causes, and implement scalable solutions.

  • Document systems, workflows, processes, and technical decisions clearly.

  • Collaborate with IT Support, IT Project Management, and other teams on escalated cases and cross-team projects.

What you’ll need to succeed

  • Experience in IT systems engineering, endpoint management, identity and access management, or a closely related field.

  • Proficiency in Okta and a solid understanding of identity and access management concepts.

  • Hands-on experience with Jamf, Google Workspace, and Slack.

  • Experience building and maintaining automated workflows with tools such as Okta Workflows, Zapier, Workato, or similar platforms.

  • Practical knowledge of macOS and Windows environments.

  • Proficiency in Bash and scripting, with the ability to automate repetitive administration tasks, integrate systems, troubleshoot issues, and maintain clear and reusable scripts.

  • Proficiency in AI tools for IT operations, automation, or productivity.

  • Experience setting up MCP servers.

  • The ability to contribute to project management and take ownership of initiatives.

  • The ability to work autonomously while collaborating effectively with others.

  • The ability to provide clear and regular progress updates on owned projects and initiatives.

  • A proactive approach to problem-solving and continuous improvement.

  • The ability to understand and follow clear guidelines and directions.

  • Professional fluency in English.

Nice-to-have

  • Some knowledge of Jira.

  • Experience with Microsoft Intune.

  • French language skills.

  • Experience contributing to internal AI, automation, or digital workplace initiatives.

If you are interested in this role, please send your CV in English.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Experimentation Interfaces
description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join

The Experimentation team's mission is to provide an insightful, reliable and easy to use experimentation platform (A/B testing and feature rollout) for customers across the company. Thousands of experiments run on our platform each year. Our team is multidisciplinary, owning UIs for setting up and analyzing experiments, data pipelines and libraries for calculating results, and clients for assignment and delivery. You will work closely with design and data science partners and with the engineers and analysts across the company who use our tools every day.

The Difference You Will Make

You will co-own the web application where teams set up, manage and analyze experiments and feature configuration, and the AI-assisted workflows that are becoming part of how experiments are designed, validated and read out. You will build features end to end, from the React/TypeScript interface through Python APIs to the data layer, and make our tools intuitive and trustworthy for users with a wide range of statistical backgrounds. Success looks like features that measurably speed up experiment setup and readout, and AI-enabled tools that people adopt because they are reliable.

A Typical Day

  • Work with design and key customers to shape intuitive experiences, including how to visualize experiment results so users with minimal statistical training draw good conclusions.
  • Build AI-enabled workflows for our users, such as agent tools and skills that help create, validate and analyze experiments, and the interface around them, with evaluations that keep quality high.
  • Use AI-assisted development to move faster, and help the team set good practice for it.
  • Work with data science partners to bring new methodology into the product.
  • Participate in experiment reviews to understand how customers use the platform and where it falls short.

Your Expertise

  • 5+ years in a hands-on software engineering role, shipping high-quality code to production, including full-stack web applications on a modern stack.
  • Strong front-end skills: React and TypeScript fundamentals, state and data fetching, performance and testing, and a good eye for intuitive interfaces in data-rich or enterprise tools.
  • Experience across the stack: backend APIs in Python or a similar language, GraphQL or comparable API design, and relational database storage.
  • Hands-on experience with AI: you build with LLMs or agent tooling (tools, skills, evaluations), or you are fluent with AI-assisted development and know how to verify what it produces.
  • Experience working directly with customers and design to turn ambiguous needs into shipped, well-designed features, with clear communication.
  • [Bonus] Experience with data visualization or data-intensive applications.
  • [Bonus] Experience with experimentation platforms.

Our Commitment To Inclusion & Belonging:

Airbnb is committed to working with the broadest talent pool possible. We believe diverse ideas foster innovation and engagement, and allow us to attract creatively-led people, and to develop the best products, services and solutions. All qualified individuals are encouraged to apply.

We strive to also provide a disability inclusive application and interview process. If you are a candidate with a disability and require reasonable accommodation in order to submit an application, please contact us at: reasonableaccommodations@airbnb.com. Please include your full name, the role you’re applying for and the accommodation necessary to assist you with the recruiting process.

We ask that you only reach out to us if you are a candidate whose disability prevents you from being able to complete our online application.

Reasonable Accommodations: We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process for applicants with disabilities. If you need assistance, or an accommodation, please let your recruiter know once you are contacted about a role.
